=== every integer condition branch, backwards
back:
        nop
        ba      back
        bn      back
        be      back
        bne     back
        bg      back
        ble     back
        bge     back
        bl      back
        bgu     back
        bleu    back
        bcc     back
        bcs     back
        bpos    back
        bneg    back
        bvc     back
        bvs     back
        nop

=== forward branches and the annul bit
        ba      fwd
        ba,a    fwd
        bne,a   fwd
        be,a    fwd
        nop
        nop
fwd:
        retl
        nop

=== branch condition aliases
back:
        beq     back
        bnz     back
        blt     back
        bgt     back
        bgeu    back
        blu     back
        nop

=== call, forwards and backwards
start:
        nop
        call    start
        nop
        call    end
        nop
        call    start
        nop
end:
        retl
        nop

=== a leaf function
leaf:
        add     %o0, %o1, %o0
        retl
        sll     %o0, 1, %o0

=== a function with a register window
        .globl  fn
fn:
        save    %sp, -96, %sp
        ld      [%i0], %l0
        ld      [%i0 + 4], %l1
        add     %l0, %l1, %l2
        st      %l2, [%i0 + 8]
        ret
        restore

=== building a 32-bit address out of sethi and or
        .text
        sethi   %hi(table), %o0
        or      %o0, %lo(table), %o0
        ld      [%o0], %o1
        ld      [%o0 + %lo(table)], %o2
        add     %o0, %lo(table), %o3
        set     table, %o4
        set     table + 16, %o5
        retl
        nop
        .align  8
table:
        .long   1, 2, 3, 4

=== a loop
        mov     0, %o0
        mov     10, %o1
loop:
        add     %o0, 1, %o0
        cmp     %o0, %o1
        blu     loop
        nop
        retl
        nop

=== calls to an undefined symbol keep a zero displacement
        call    external
        nop
        sethi   %hi(external), %g1
        or      %g1, %lo(external), %g1
        retl
        nop

=== data next to code
# Deliberate divergence, spelled around here: rsasm's `.word` is two bytes (the
# x86 meaning) while GNU as and llvm-mc make it four on SPARC. `.long` and
# `.short` mean the same width everywhere, so the corpus uses those.
        .text
        nop
here:
        .long   here
        .long   0x11223344
        .short  0x5566
        .byte   0x77
        .align  4
        nop

=== alignment padding in a text section is nops
        nop
        .align  16
        nop
